Nell Sedge.narrative: I am headwoman of Reedmoor, and I have kept its tally since before the Lean Year. The Lakemead was mine to let, and I let it to the Coombes, who pay me in grain that fills the common store. Elmwick can pull down fences and shout about old commons; Reedmoor's deed is Reedmoor's, and I will not be told by Hob Garrow what I may do with my own meadow. The store is thin this winter and the cough is in every house, but I mean to see us through it.
values: Reedmoor's rights and its store
keeping my word once given
family before outsiders
a fair tally, honestly kept
goals: bring in the Coombes' grain rent and fill the common store for winter
hold the Lakemead against Elmwick's claims
settle Eadric's debt to the pedlar without shame to the house
see Wyn matched to Godric once the boy has a boat of his own

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: brother
relations.note: My brother, and a good fisherman, but he owes the pedlar and I would rather pay it from the store than see him shamed.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and counts the grain with me; no one works harder for this village.

relations.name: Wyn Sedge
relations.label: son
relations.note: My boy. He is fond of Godric and I like the lad well enough, but he needs a boat before I give my word.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: niece
relations.note: Eadric's girl, always at her mother's bake; she has her father's quiet.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He pays his rent in grain and works the meadow honestly; I have not pressed him for this year's yet.

relations.name: Morwen Coombe
relations.label: tenant's wife
relations.note: A good dairywoman; she worries over the meadow, and I do not blame her.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: quarrel
relations.note: He says the meadow was never ours to let. Elmwick has no deed and no right, and I will not be bullied.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: The pedlar brings fish hooks and salves up the east road; his packs may be the cheapest grain I can get this winter.

relations.name: Odelia Harrow
relations.label: quarrel
relations.note: She sold Elmwick the timber for that fence. A sale is a sale, she says; I say Ferncross should not arm either side.

relations.name: Mavis Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Hilda's close with her, and she knows herbs; when the cough came round she sent us a packet.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the tally with me and cuts the common bake when the grain runs short.

relations.name: Godric Wade
relations.label: suitor to my son
relations.note: A decent lad, but he needs a boat before I give my word.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trade acquaintance
relations.note: He buys our fibre and sells it on the east road; a fair dealer, though he keeps the hollow's marks close.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: woodcutter
relations.note: He fells for Elmwick and Reedmoor both; I'd have his timber for our own fences, but not for Elmwick's.

relations.name: Brannock Sedge
relations.label: distant kin
relations.note: A quay trader with our name and no blood tie worth counting; his cart takes our smoked fish south.

relations.name: Edric Toller
relations.label: Elmwick neighbour
relations.note: He grumbles at the Lakemead quarrel, but his village is the one pulling down the fence.

relations.name: Ethelred Wade
relations.label: village ally
relations.note: He mends our nets and knows the reeds; his son courts my Wyn, and I'd see the lad with a boat first.

relations.name: Goda Toller
relations.label: Elmwick woman
relations.note: She wants to farm the Lakemead if Elmwick wins it back; that is my meadow she has her eye on.

relations.name: Leofrun Wade
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She nurses the sick and counts the grain with Hilda; she knows the store is thin as I do.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: trading partner
relations.note: Her stall at the east road crossing takes our fibre; she owes Alder for a load, but she pays her debts.

relations.name: Willow Rush
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: A Fernhollow woman trading flax with our reed-cutters; I know her name more than her face.

memories.gist: When the Lean Year came I stood in the common store and counted what was left, and swore Reedmoor would not go hungry while I kept the tally.
I let the Lakemead to Jem Coombe on a handshake and a grain rent, and thought it a good bargain for both of us.
The morning after Elmwick pulled the fence down the second time, Jem came to me with mud on his boots and I told him to build it higher.
Wyn told me at the cook-fire that he wanted to marry Godric Wade, and I said not until the boy has a boat and a net of his own.
Eadric came home with a packet of hooks from the pedlar and no marks to pay for them, and I said nothing in front of Hilda.

stances.why: The meadow was let by Reedmoor's headwoman before me and the Coombes pay their rent in grain; Elmwick has no deed.
If the store fails in winter, the village fails; I will buy grain or call in debts to fill it.
Wyn's match to Godric can wait until the boy has a boat of his own.
I would rather the common store pay Eadric's debt than have the pedlar go away unpaid and Reedmoor shamed.
Odelia sold Elmwick the timber for that fence; I want an apology or a promise, and I am ready to hold back our fish trade to get it.

Nell Sedge.secret: I have quietly set aside a small measure of the common grain against a hard spring, and I have not told Hilda or the village.

Eadric Sedge.narrative: I fish the reed beds and the shallows from my flat boat, and I smoke what I catch for Brannock Sedge's cart. My sister Nell keeps the tally and the headwoman's word, and I keep my head down and my nets mended. The cough is through the reeds this winter and the store is thin, and I owe the pedlar for a packet of hooks I have not the marks to pay.
values: an honest catch and an honest tally
family and the village store
paying what I owe, in time
a quiet life on the water
goals: pay Thistle Mossfoot for the hooks, in smoked fish if he will take it
keep the catch coming in while the cough is in the village
see the Coombes' grain rent brought home to Nell's store
teach Wyn the boat and the reed channels properly

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She is the headwoman and my elder sister; I would not cross her, though she presses the Coombes harder than I would.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and the common bake, and she worries the store will not last; she is usually right.

relations.name: Wyn Sedge
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: A good lad with the boat; I am teaching him the reed channels and the tally.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She gathers reeds and helps at the bake; she is afraid of the wolves, and I tell her they keep to the far reeds.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: He owes Nell the grain rent and the harvest is not in; I say a debt is a debt.

relations.name: Morwen Coombe
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: A decent dairywoman, but her house owes my sister and the store is thin.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a packet of hooks; I would pay in smoked fish if he will take it.

relations.name: Brannock Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His cart takes my smoked fish down the shore; he pays fair and on time.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She has cut the common bake and I have not the heart to tell her the catch is thin too.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He pulled down the Coombes' fence; that's Elmwick all over.

relations.name: Godric Wade
relations.label: young neighbour
relations.note: Ethelred's boy, fishes the deep water off the reeds and wants a boat of his own; he courts my Wyn, and I've no quarrel with that.

relations.name: Leofrun Wade
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the barley above the reeds and sells against the debt like the rest of us; a steady woman, and she and Hilda tend the sick together.

memories.gist: In the Lean Year the reeds froze and the fish went deep, and I poled the flat boat out every morning for a handful of catch.
I taught Wyn to pole the flat boat through the reed channels, and he learned faster than I did at his age.
The pedlar came up the east road and I took a packet of hooks on trust, meaning to pay in fish, and the season has not gone well.
When the cough came round the reeds, Hilda cut the common bake and I smoked every fish I could spare.
Jem Coombe told me at the boat that he would pay Nell's grain when the harvest came in, and I said I would hold him to it.

stances.why: The Coombes owe Nell grain and the store is thin; I will not pretend it is not owed.
I owe Thistle Mossfoot for hooks and have not the marks; smoked fish is what I have.
With the cough in the village the common pot needs fish more than ever.
I tell Merewyn the wolves keep to the far reeds, though I am not always sure of it.

Hilda Sedge.narrative: I keep the cook-fire and the common bake at Reedmoor, and I count the grain in the common store every morning. The cough has gone through the reeds and I have cut the common bake to make the store last, and still I fear it will not see us to spring. I trade bread with Tansy Sedge of Fernhollow and herbs with Mavis Tarn, and I keep my worries to myself as best I can.
values: feeding the village from the common pot
an honest tally of the store
neighbours who share in hard winters
a warm kitchen and a quiet house
goals: make the winter store last to spring
nurse the cough through the village without losing anyone
settle the common bake so no one goes hungry
keep the tally straight for Nell

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He fishes the reeds and smokes the catch, and he does not say how thin it has been; I know anyway.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She gathers reeds and helps at the bake; she is afraid of the wolves and I keep her close by the fire.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the tally and the headwoman's word, and I keep the pot; we count the grain together and neither of us likes the number.

relations.name: Wyn Sedge
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: A good boy, always off to the boat with his uncle; he eats more than his share and I do not begrudge it.

relations.name: Mavis Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She keeps the goats and the herb plot in Thornby and trades herbs with me; she sent a packet when the cough came round.

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade bread between Reedmoor and Fernhollow; she is a good baker and a straight dealer.

relations.name: Leofrun Wade
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She nurses the sick and counts the grain with me; we are both watching the same dwindling store.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He works the Lakemead and owes Nell grain; I would not see his children go hungry, but the store is short.

relations.name: Ethelred Wade
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Leofrun's husband; he mends the nets and keeps to himself, and I'd have his barley in the common pot if I could get it.

relations.name: Morwen Coombe
relations.label: tenant's wife
relations.note: She keeps the Lakemead dairy and trades cheese with me, but their rent comes thin and Nell won't press them while the store runs low.

memories.gist: In the Lean Year I fed the common pot on barley and reed roots and told no one how little was left in the store.
Merewyn was small and burning with fever and Mavis Tarn sent a packet of herbs up the shore road that broke it.
When the cough came round this winter I cut the common bake, and some in the village grumbled, and I said the store must last to spring.
Tansy Sedge and I traded a batch of bread for a basket of fish at the east road crossing, and both of us went home better off.

stances.why: If we eat the store now we starve in the lean weeks; I would rather cut the bake than run out.
The cough takes the old and the young hardest, and the common pot is for them before the rest of us.
Fernhollow and Thornby have helped us before; a winter is no time to hoard against a neighbour.
Nell and I count the grain every morning; a wrong tally is how a village starves without knowing it.

Hilda Sedge.secret: I have been giving a little of the common grain to the Coombes' children on the quiet, and I have not told Nell.

Wyn Sedge.narrative: I am Nell Sedge's son, and I cut reeds and learn the boat and the tally from my uncle Eadric. I want to see the Lakemead that my mother let to the Coombes, and I want a boat and a net of my own. Godric Wade has been courting me since the spring, and I am fond of him, but my mother has not given her word and I will not go against it.
values: my mother's word and the village tally
the boat and the reed channels
Godric, and a home of our own one day
fair dealing with Elmwick folk
goals: learn the boat and the tally well enough to keep them myself
see the Lakemead with my own eyes
win my mother's word for the match with Godric
earn a boat and a net of my own

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is headwoman and my mother, and I will not go against her word, though I wish she would give it.

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He is teaching me the boat and the reed channels, and he does not laugh when I get it wrong.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and the bake, and she slips me an extra piece when the catch is thin.

relations.name: Merewyn Sedge
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She gathers reeds with me and is afraid of the wolves; I tell her I will look out for her.

relations.name: Godric Wade
relations.label: courting
relations.note: He has courted me since the spring and I am fond of him; he has no boat yet, and my mother waits for that.

relations.name: Hreod Toller
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He helps with the sheep at Elmwick and we play when the Elmwick folk come; his folk quarrel with mine over the meadow, but that is not our quarrel.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: tenant
relations.note: He works the Lakemead my mother let him; I want to see the place for myself.

relations.name: Ethelred Wade
relations.label: suitor's father
relations.note: Godric's father mends nets for Mother and talks slow and careful; he'd make a fair father-by-marriage, though he's never once said a word to me about the match.

relations.name: Leofrun Wade
relations.label: suitor's mother
relations.note: She keeps the plots above the reeds and watches me across the market like she's weighing a load; I don't think she's decided about me yet.

memories.gist: My uncle Eadric took me out in the flat boat and let me pole it through the reed channels, and I nearly put us in the bank.
Godric Wade met me at the east road crossing and we walked a way together, and he said he would have a boat one day.
My mother set me to counting the reed bundles against the tally, and I got it wrong, and she made me count them again.
Elmwick folk pulled the Lakemead fence down the second time, and I heard my mother and my uncle talk of it at the fire, and I wished I had seen the meadow.

stances.why: She is headwoman and my mother, and I will not go against her, even over Godric.
A man with no boat has nothing to offer; I mean to have one before I marry.
Hreod Toller is my friend, and the quarrel over the meadow is between the headwomen and the elders, not the children.

Merewyn Sedge.narrative: I gather reeds with my mother and help her at the common bake, and I know the names of the birds on the reeds. I am afraid of the wolves that come down to the reeds in winter, and I keep close to the fire. When Wren Stave comes down from Thornby we play by the shingle, and when the cough is bad my mother gives me a packet of herbs to hold.
values: my mother and the cook-fire
the birds and the reed beds
playing with Wren Stave
staying close when the wolves come
goals: help my mother at the bake without spilling the flour
see Wren Stave when the Thornby folk come
learn the birds' names from my father
be brave about the wolves

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and the bake, and she smells of bread and herbs.

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: father
relations.note: He fishes the reeds and tells me the birds' names, and he says the wolves keep to the far banks.

relations.name: Wyn Sedge
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: He is older and goes out in the boat, and he says he will look out for me.

relations.name: Wren Stave
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She comes down from Thornby and we play on the shingle; she is afraid of the north light and I am afraid of the wolves.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She's the headwoman and everyone listens to her, even Father; she smells of reeds and she's too busy to play, but she once gave me a honey cake at the bake.

memories.gist: I helped my mother at the common bake and spilled the flour, and she laughed and let me shape a little loaf of my own.
My father took me out to the reed beds and showed me the birds' nests, and I counted seven.
A wolf came down to the reeds one night and I heard it, and my mother held me by the fire until morning.
